correctness.rationale: Convex side follows from feasible-set inclusion and strict convexity. On the indefinite side exact Taylor expansion gives ell=y and q=-xy; the SQP optimum is (r,0), with q=0. The unconstrained optimum (r,m) is strictly SQCQP-feasible for r>1,m>0, yielding gap m²/2 and distance m. Negative multiplier m/(1-r) proves the SQP point is not SQCQP stationary. Hessian eigenvalues ±1 and base gradient norm one are verified algebraically. 16,269 exact-rational witness tests and nine convex controls supplement, not replace, the quantified proof.

value.rationale: The source proposes a scalar curvature probe to decide whether a costly quadratic constraint model is needed. The new result supplies the natural convex-sufficiency boundary and an opposite worst case: zero scalar probe correction fails even first-order KKT conditions of the quadratic model and misses an arbitrarily better minimizer, despite bounded constraint curvature, regular linearization, exact derivatives, and matched identity quadratic objective matrices. This is a substantive directional-information limitation relevant to nonconvex model selection, not just a scaling or sign error.
